To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size and location of Pt clusters formed in PtY zeolites depend on the conditions following ion exchange, i.e., the temperature of calcination and reduction and the presence of auxiliary transition metal ions.

(1) calcination at temperatures above 500°C promotes the migration of platinum ions from supercage to sodalite cage, (2) this migration can be suppressed by filling the sodalite cage with auxiliary ions of different transition metals, and (3) the location of Pt ions determines whether small clusters or large particles form during reduction.
the location of Pt ions in the zeolite cages determines the size and location of the Pt particles after reduction.

the preparation of transition metal clusters by ion-exchange, their characterization, and the elucidation of their catalytic activity.
